QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_13

question.text: The NAV of a Cat III open-ended AIF scheme must be calculated and disclosed to investors at a minimum frequency of:

explanation.text: The Logic: For Cat III OPEN-ENDED schemes the NAV must be disclosed to investors at MONTHLY intervals (close-ended Cat III funds disclose quarterly). Daily NAV is usual for funds investing only in listed securities, but the regulatory disclosure floor for open-ended schemes is monthly. The Trap: Daily is operational norm but not the regulatory disclosure floor. Weekly is a made-up middle ground. Quarterly is the rule for CLOSE-ENDED Cat III. Note: The workbook supports the monthly/quarterly regulatory floor; recommendations on daily LP publishing or side-pocket trigger workflows are not part of the syllabus.
